data.name: Joram
data.gender_notes: Joram is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew roots 'yad' (hand) and 'ram' (exalted, high), Joram symbolizes a strong, God-given leader. In the Bible, Joram was the name of two kings of Judah and Israel. King Joram of Judah, also known as Joram son of Jehoshaphat, ruled during a time of peace and prosperity. King Joram of Israel, also known as Joram son of Ahab, was a wicked king who led his people into rebellion against God.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents God's divine guidance and strength.
data.etymology: Joram belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Joram total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

For instance, it appears as a character name in Mark Twain's "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn." Its appearance in such diverse cultural contexts suggests its association with strong leadership and influence.
data.spiritual_significance: Joram is a reminder of the power and potential inherent in each of us. The name's Hebrew origins symbolize the idea that with God's help, we can be exalted leaders and overcome even the greatest obstacles. Additionally, the biblical stories of Joram the righteous and Joram the wicked serve as cautionary tales, reminding us of the importance of living in accordance with God's will and avoiding the pitfalls of pride and wickedness.
